audit.whatIsWrong: Chart read Skill / Vladimir / Vladimir / Skill / Skill / Vladimir / Vladimir while the prose on both layers describes Karma owning levels 1 through first item and only losing at 2+ items.
audit.why: Packet levelChart is Karma, Karma, Karma, Karma, Skill, Karma, Vladimir, and the 56.41% win rate over 39 games is a Karma-favoured lane. Difficulty 5.5/10 overstated the threat.
audit.corrected: Both layers set to the packet chart; diffRating dropped to 4.5/10.

audit.whatIsWrong: Full-layer phase whys were champion boilerplate and named no Vladimir spike.
audit.why: His real curve is a famously weak level 1 (Transfusion only, 9s at rank 1), Sanguine Pool coming online as an all-in dodge, and Rylai's/Liandry's at two items where his sustain beats Karma's chip. Karma has no level-6 spike since Mantra exists from level 1.
audit.corrected: Rewrote phases[0..6].why around Transfusion's cooldown, Pool, and the two-item flip.

audit.whatIsWrong: breakdown.cooldowns gave Sanguine Pool no number and never stated that it blanks Focused Resolve.
audit.why: Pool is 28/25/22/19/16s and grants 2 seconds of untargetability. Karma's W (Focused Resolve) is a tether that must survive to root, so Pool cancels the root outright — that is the decisive interaction of the matchup.
audit.corrected: Stated the untargetability window, the real cooldowns, and 'bait it with a Q first'.

audit.whatIsWrong: Anti-heal was mentioned only as a trailing clause in the itemization line, with no timing.
audit.why: Vladimir sustains through chip damage via Transfusion and Hemoplague's per-champion heal; Karma's whole plan is chip damage, so Grievous Wounds timing decides every extended trade.
audit.corrected: Added the anti-heal trigger to breakdown.cooldowns so it sits next to the sequencing advice.

edits.before: Q poke at level 1 is among the best in the game — chunk Vladimir on every last-hit and start the Mantra economy.
edits.after: Vlad has no Pool yet and one of the worst level 1s — open RQ Soulflare on his first last-hit and chunk him.

edits.before: W tether threatens the root — anyone who steps to you early eats Q-W and donates the trade.
edits.after: Poke on the cooldown of his 9s Transfusion — Gathering Fire refunds Mantra faster than he heals.

edits.before: Full kit: E shield-speed makes you untouchable in short trades. Mantra-Q (RQ) on cooldown gaps is a third of his HP.
edits.after: RQ Soulflare's delayed zone and slow chunk Vlad off the wave — until Sanguine Pool is leveled he has no answer.

edits.before: Spam the RQ slow-field on his farming spots and keep your shield for Sanguine Pool — the lane is a toll booth and you own it.
edits.after: Your 4-5 peak: repeated Q/RQ rotations shove him under tower and you tax plates behind Inspire's speed before he buys sustain.

edits.before: No new ultimate at 6 — your Mantra has been online since level 1. His spike is the danger window: respect it.
edits.after: Level 6 is even — your R has been online since 1, while Pool now drops targetability and blanks your W root.

edits.before: First item amplifies the RQ chunk — keep him under 60% and the lane stays yours by default.
edits.after: Your first AP/haste item sharpens RQ burst and shield value — a strong poke window before he spikes.

edits.before: You drift toward utility now — peel, shield, and speed your carries while the RQ poke softens objectives.
edits.after: Post-Rylai/Liandry he out-sustains your chip and Tides of Blood bursts you — close it out before two items.

edits.before: - Vladimir Sanguine Pool: matchup-defining — Untargetable dodge — bait it before you spend your kill window. Read it like a second minimap. - Guard your E shield like a fifth summoner spell. - Ultimate goes to kill windows only.
edits.after: - Sanguine Pool: 28s at rank 1, 16s at rank 5 — 2s untargetable that blanks your W root, so bait it with a Q first. - Transfusion is his only sustain: buy anti-heal before it out-paces your chip. - Commit Mantra only on Pool's downtime.

notes: Both layers already agreed with each other but both disagreed with the packet chart and with their own prose; fixed in matched pairs. Left diff as EVEN rather than inventing a new enum token, and lowered diffRating instead. Tides of Blood is blockable by enemy units per Riot's text (it 'can be blocked by enemy units') — worth a future line about standing behind minions, but I had no length budget to add it without cutting verified content.
